page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. In stress-ng tests, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance rank in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show similar constraints, with read-only large block transfers falling into the bottom 10% and write operations in the bottom 25%. Computational workloads, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also register in the bottom 10% for single-threaded execution. These results reflect the older architectural generation of the underlying Intel Broadwell processor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2ne.xlarge offers dedicated CPU allocation without the resource sharing typical of burstable instances, which ensures predictable, albeit modest, performance. The primary tradeoff is the lower performance-per-resource ratio compared to newer hardware generations. It serves as a cost-effective option for legacy applications or development environments that require dedicated CPU cores but do not demand high-throughput memory or advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI.

This instance is recommended for lightweight general-purpose workloads. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, development and testing environments, small-scale database operations, and low-traffic application hosting. It is less suitable for high-performance computing, large-scale data processing, or real-time machine learning inference due to its limited memory bandwidth and older CPU architecture.
